## 8. Models

### Pencil Hatching (`lumenary:pencil-hatching`, models this process)

_From: Illustration, engraving and drawing; when: Renaissance onward; works best on: Objects and portraits with strong form._

An illustrator builds tone from layers of parallel strokes: one set in one direction, a second across it, more where the shadow is deepest. A light area has none, a mid tone has one set and the deepest shadow is crossed four times. This treatment stacks up to four layers at different angles, each appearing only once the picture is dark enough.

**How it is made, as the model does it:**

1. Set up to four layers of strokes at 45, 135, 0 and 90 degrees, all turned together by the turn slider.
2. Let a layer appear only when the darkness passes its threshold of 0.16, 0.34, 0.54 or 0.74.
3. For each layer, divide the position across the strokes by the line spacing, with slow noise for the hand’s wobble, and take the integer part as the stroke index.
4. Make each stroke thicker the further the darkness is past the threshold, with its own random width and pressure seeded by its index.
5. Combine layers by taking the strongest, lighten with paper tooth, and add optional soft outlines.

**The maths:**

$$u_k=\frac{x\cos\theta_k+y\sin\theta_k}{s}+2.4\,\omega\,\big(\nu-\tfrac12\big),\qquad f=u_k-\lfloor u_k\rfloor$$

_s is the line spacing, ω the hand wobble, ν slow noise; ⌊u⌋ is the stroke number and f the place inside it._ (primitives: tone-line-screen, smooth-noise)

$$w_k=\operatorname{clip}\!\big(3.2\,(d-t_k)+0.2,\ 0,\ 0.96\big),\qquad t=(0.16,\ 0.34,\ 0.54,\ 0.74)$$

_Stroke width grows with how far the darkness d is past the layer’s threshold._ (primitives: tone-line-screen)

$$a=\max_{k}\Big[\big(1-\operatorname{smoothstep}(w_k-0.28,\ w_k,\ \lvert 2f-1\rvert)\big)\,\pi_k\Big]$$

_Ink coverage at the pixel; π_k is the random pressure (0.62 to 1) of its stroke in layer k._ (primitives: tone-line-screen, seeded-random)

**Dials:** `space` (Line spacing) = 5.5 [3 to 12]; `layers` (Layers of hatching) = 4 [2 to 4]; `angle` (Turn the hatching) = 0 [0 to 90]; `wobble` (Hand wobble) = 40 [0 to 100]; `outline` (Soft outlines) = true; `lead` (Pencil) = "graphite" (graphite, sepia, blue, red); `paper` (Paper) = "cream" (white, cream, grey).

**History:** Hatching and cross-hatching were developed in drawing and engraving long before photography, by artists such as Albrecht Dürer, who used them to model form in prints. Graphite was found at Borrowdale in England in the 1560s, and the modern pencil followed. Today hatching is used in comics, manga, technical illustration and architectural sketches.
